claims.title: Exact finite-horizon active-experiment frontier under one globally fixed probabilistic model
claims.scope: finite fixed-model families, finite rational experiment menus, exact rational observation kernels and acquisition costs, deterministic zero-error prefix-code actions, and finite horizon
assumptions: one model is selected once and remains fixed for the full horizon
the experiment is chosen before the current public observation and the code after it
code actions do not alter hidden-state transitions
all candidate, continuation, frontier, and dominance searches complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the theorem does not estimate experiment kernels or model families from data
the bounded solver is not a polynomial-time scalability guarantee
the result is not evidence for simulation

claims.title: Source-independent public observations can strictly improve deterministic minimax coding through public randomization alone
claims.scope: finite minimax coding policies where a public observation has the same distribution under every hidden state and every fixed model
assumptions: the public observation is available before the deterministic code action
all decoders observe the same public signal
the source-independent signal is admitted as a coordination resource
nonclaims: decision improvement from such a signal is not epistemic information about the model
the theorem does not claim every uninformative signal is useful

claims.title: Adding an available experiment cannot worsen the exact minimizing fixed-model controller
claims.scope: two finite experiment menus with one contained in the other and otherwise identical model family, code universe, horizon, and costs
assumptions: the controller may ignore newly added experiments
the outer objective remains minimum over policies of maximum expected cost across one fixed model
nonclaims: adding an experiment need not improve value strictly
the result does not price external implementation complexity omitted from acquisition cost

claims.title: Persistent fixed-model identity creates multi-period option value for early model information
claims.scope: finite-horizon active experiment policies where one latent model remains fixed across all periods
assumptions: public histories may condition future experiment and code choices
the same model generates current and future signals and source laws
experiment acquisition cost is additive and declared
nonclaims: the theorem does not assert that early sensing is always optimal
the option value depends on persistence, horizon, experiment quality, and cost

claims.title: K3 no-signal, public-randomness, and full-revelation values are two, five-thirds, and one
claims.scope: three globally fixed one-state point-mass K3 models over one period with respectively no signal, a source-independent uniform three-way public signal, and a model-revealing signal
assumptions: complete binary zero-error prefix codes have length vectors that are permutations of (1,2,2)
experiment acquisition costs are zero
nonclaims: the one-third and two-thirds decomposition is specific to this symmetric finite instance
the public-randomness gain is not evidence that the signal learned the model

claims.title: Randomness-matched K3 sensing threshold is two-thirds
claims.scope: the K3 public-coin baseline compared with a fully model-revealing one-period experiment carrying additive acquisition cost kappa
assumptions: the public coin is available at zero cost
tie-breaking selects the lexicographically earlier public-coin experiment at equality
nonclaims: the threshold differs if the baseline excludes public randomization
the acquisition cost is an abstract declared quantity

claims.title: Three-period persistent K3 revelation at cost three-halves lowers robust value from five to nine-halves
claims.scope: three globally fixed point-mass K3 models, three periods, free no-signal experiment, and a perfectly revealing experiment costing 3/2
assumptions: the revealing experiment is run before a code action
once a public history excludes other models, that model identity remains fixed in later periods
nonclaims: the exact values are specific to the finite K3 construction
the example is not an empirical estimate of real sensing value

claims.title: Bounded exact active-experiment and information-randomness audit
claims.scope: the K3 no-signal, public-randomness, revealing-signal, acquisition-threshold, persistent-horizon, monotonicity, and cap instances exercised by repository tests
assumptions: all exact-rational policy combinations and Pareto dominance checks complete below configured caps
all experiment kernels, source laws, and costs are represented with exact Fraction arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded finite tests are not a continuous-model theorem
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation
